behavior.arguments: rdi = struct pointer; fields read and written: flag qword at [rdi], source qword at [rdi+0x50], destination qword at [rdi+0x58]. No other argument register is read.

edges.all_ones_flag: flag all-ones, source 0, dest 0 -> flag cleared, dest unchanged, rax 0.
edges.both_effects: flag 7, source 5, dest 3 -> flag cleared and dest synced to 5, rax 5.
edges.flag_only: flag 7, source 5, dest 5 -> flag cleared only, rax 5.
edges.noop: flag 0, source 5, dest 5 -> no change, rax 5.
edges.sync_only: flag 0, source 5, dest 3 -> sync only, rax 5.
edges.sync_to_nonzero: flag 0, source 9, dest 0 -> dest synced to 9, rax 9.
edges.sync_to_zero: flag 3, source 0, dest 9 -> flag cleared and dest synced to 0, rax 0.

behavior.entry_shape: Straight-line sync with two forward branches and one ret; no loop, no call opcode inside the window.
behavior.return_observation: At ret, rax holds the loaded [rdi+0x50] value on both paths. This is an observed register state, not a claimed return contract; the callers' use of it is not claimed.
behavior.return_rule: If qword [rdi] is nonzero, set it to 0. Then load qword [rdi+0x50]; if it differs from qword [rdi+0x58], set [rdi+0x58] to it.
behavior.weakness: The two effects read as unrelated housekeeping; nothing in the bytes links the flag qword to the synced fields. The window is bound only because both effects lock exactly from its own bytes, not because they are shown to belong to one operation.

caller_fdes.note: Site confirmed as an instruction start by linear disassembly from the caller FDE start; caller setup immediately before the call is lea 0x10(%rsp),%rdi; caller purpose not claimed.
Site confirmed as an instruction start by linear disassembly from the caller FDE start; caller setup immediately before the call is mov -0x310(%rbp),%rdi; caller purpose not claimed.

coordinate_system: ELF virtual addresses, without a guessed loader or Ghidra rebase. The ELF section table maps .text with file offset = VA - 0x1000; the retained .eh_frame has equal file offset and VA. The tools resolve sections rather than assuming one global VA/file-offset relationship.

incoming_pattern_scan.note: Byte-pattern scan over the full .text section (70,370,352 bytes) for e8 sites whose rel32 lands on the window start; every site was additionally confirmed as an instruction start by linear disassembly from its caller FDE start. This is explicitly not a complete xref census: indirect calls, tail jumps, and PLT references are out of scope for the scan.

scout_corrections: The round-12 scout note listed this window (ranked #3) with FDE [0x5172fa0, 0x5172fc0), 32 bytes, 0 padding bytes, two direct callers both boundary-confirmed, and no naming relocation. Every element verified exactly, including the zero-padding boundary and the nearest claimed window (tiny two-byte gate 0x51647b0, packet #72, 0xe7f0 away). No numeric correction to the scout's numbers was needed. One phrasing point is reconciled explicitly: the scout's 'zero calls' describes the window body (no call opcode inside it), while the two direct sites are incoming calls from two caller FDEs — the two statements are about different directions and do not conflict.
